They are legally distinct entities in some contexts — Endress+Hauser Japan Co., Ltd. is the sales company, and the Yamanashi facility is where the flow lab is located. They are genuinely different legal entity names — "Japan" vs "Yamanashi" is not spelling drift or suffix drift; it's a different company name denoting a different (related) legal entity.

The rules say: "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)."

Is "Endress + Hauser Japan Co., Ltd" vs "Endress+Hauser Yamanashi Co., Ltd." genuinely different? Yes — Japan vs Yamanashi is a substantive difference in the entity name, not a spelling/suffix/accent drift. The certificate is the legal instrument, so the applicant on the certificate is what matters. So verdict: different-entity, best_value = "Endress+Hauser Yamanashi Co., Ltd."

However, one could argue that Endress+Hauser Yamanashi Co., Ltd. is a renamed version of Endress+Hauser Japan Co., Ltd.? Let me check: Endress+Hauser Japan Co., Ltd. is based in Tokyo (Akasaka). Historically, in 2021 there might have been a merger: Endress+Hauser Yamanashi Co., Ltd. merged into Endress+Hauser Japan Co., Ltd. and the legal entity was renamed "Endress+Hauser Japan Co., Ltd." Hmm. Actually I recall: "Endress+Hauser (Japan) Co., Ltd." — the sales center in Tokyo. The manufacturing is "Endress+Hauser Yamanashi Co., Ltd." In 2022, Endress+Hauser Japan and Endress+Hauser Yamanashi merged into "Endress+Hauser Japan Co., Ltd." possibly. But at the time of the certificate (2020), they'd be distinct entities.

Regardless, per the rules: different company names = different-entity, best_value = document's. This is not spelling drift — "Japan" vs "Yamanashi" are different words. So different-entity.
